Mood Board

1,220 sq ft · 2 bed / 3 bath

A black-and-white checkerboard floor, set on the diagonal, runs through the entire home — bedrooms, living room, kitchen, dining room, entryways, closets — at one consistent size throughout, stopping at the stairs (reclaimed wood treads) and all three bathrooms, which take a small-format charcoal mosaic floor instead, paired with sea-glass-look tiled walls and matte black hardware. Walk-in closets throughout get built-in cabinetry and organizer systems. Both bedrooms get a wood-look tile accent wall behind the headboard, the same tile carried into the entryway. The downstairs powder room is converted into a full bath laid out as a curbless wet room.

A note on flexibility. The one must-have is the checkerboard tile throughout. Everything else — colors, materials, fixtures, and how to get the best value — is genuinely open to the design firm's judgment. This is a starting reference, not a locked spec. The general aesthetic direction we're after: fresh and current, the kind of space that photographs well today, but grounded enough in timeless choices that it won't read as dated in five or ten years.

Bathrooms

Six wall tile options compared for the three bathrooms — on reflectance, price, format, and how each pairs with the bathroom floor: Dawson, Charcoal, a near-neutral dark gray at 30.4% reflectance and 5.6% saturation. Leona's checkerboard values (≈85% white, ≈16% black, both warm) are marked on the chart for reference alongside Dawson. Lilah, Opal is the preferred look, specified throughout this book. Format deltas below are noted against Jaden, Hunter.

By Room
Primary Bedroom

Two separate twin beds give the kids who sleep here their own space, each with its own Thuma Pedestal Side Table, Walnut — the same nightstand used in the secondary bedroom. The 13-foot wall behind both headboards is wrapped floor to ceiling in the same wood-look plank tile used on the entryway wall, run vertically in 13 columns to pull the eye up — a durable, wipeable surface right where the beds make contact. Checkerboard floor, gray walls in glossy finish elsewhere in the room. Closets stay open — doors come off, frames stay in place — fitted with built-in organizers and a built-in desktop. All hardware in matte black.

Primary Bedroom Walk-In Closet

Two walk-in closets (5' x 5.5' each) get built-in cabinetry and organizer systems in a wood-grain veneer finish stained to match Zayne's tone — the same wood language as the stair treads and accent walls — rather than base white melamine, keeping the bed's walnut distinct so it pops against the room instead of blending in. Plus a built-in desktop topped in Absolute Black granite — bundled with the dining room's granite order for durability and easy cleaning. Doors come off, frames stay in place, so both closets read open into the room. Each gets its own light fixture. Checkerboard floor, gray walls in glossy finish, matte black hardware.

Primary Bathroom

Alcove tub / tile shower with matte black drain kit, right drain, and a curved shower curtain rod. Sea-glass ceramic in a wavy glossy glaze — set in a straight 6" grid — wraps the tub surround and carries straight on down the whole wall that holds the vanity and toilet, floor to ceiling — one continuous plane. Single 36" vanity, Acorn finish, black hardware provides unobstructed width to the tub's full alcove opening. Small-format charcoal mosaic floor, matching downstairs and the secondary bath, gray walls, matte black faucet, medicine cabinet, toilet, shower head + handheld wand for tub use.

Secondary Bedroom

The 12-foot wall behind the headboard is wrapped floor to ceiling in the same wood-look plank tile used in the primary bedroom and on the entryway wall, run vertically in 12 columns. Checkerboard floor, gray walls in glossy finish elsewhere in the room for easy wipe-down. Standalone furniture — platform bed, desk, and side table, all in walnut finish. Two wall closets with matte black hardware. All interior doors and frames finished in white, for night visibility of open/closed.

Secondary Bathroom

Shower-only, no tub — the whole room takes the same small-format charcoal mosaic floor as downstairs and the primary bath, with a linear drain in the shower matching downstairs. Paired with the same blue-green glossy ceramic on the walls, set in the same straight 6" grid, wrapping the shower and continuing along the full wall that holds the vanity and toilet, floor to ceiling. A frameless sliding glass door, matte black, closes the full 60" opening. Single 30" vanity, Acorn finish, black hardware. Gray walls, matte black faucet, medicine cabinet, toilet, and a fixed shower head — no handheld wand.

No changes to white kitchen cabinetry, stainless appliances, black granite countertop, or backsplash — shown here for flooring and wall color continuity, plus two counter stools at the island (a matching pair sits at the dining-room desk stations). New window treatment on the kitchen window. Checkerboard floors, gray walls in glossy finish.

Dining Room

Checkerboard floors, gray walls in glossy finish. Kitchen cabinets and counters extend across the length of the dining room with 36" counter depth to allow use as desk space at bar stool height and space to put a coffee machine. Dining table is 36" round dining table (white marble top, matte black base), paired with 4 black ash dining chairs. A matte black aluminum bi-fold door — three panels that fold away — opens the wall to the patio.

Downstairs Bathroom

Powder room converted to a full bath: a curbless wet room split evenly into two 30.5" sections — shower to the west, toilet kept dry behind fixed glass to the east. Opal color tile runs floor-to-ceiling on three walls; only the pocket-door wall stays paint. A ceiling-mount rain head (no handheld wand — rain heads throw the least spray), the corner sink with a matte black single hole faucet and mirror above, the same Kingston toilet as elsewhere, and a 28" white pocket door, for night visibility of open/closed. A rigid support bar from the west wall braces the glass panel and doubles as the curtain rod — the curtain screens the sink and walk-in from spray when drawn.

Proposed floor plan to fit a 3/4 bath in place of the existing 1/2 bath. 30.5" x 61" = 1861 sq in

Entryway

An archway passageway wall between the living room and kitchen. A tiled accent wall — wood-look ribbed ceramic in a plank format — wraps up and over the small ceiling section above it, reading as one clean, continuous statement; the long run of wall is exactly what the plank proportion and relief texture need to shine. Optional: a shoe storage bench along the wall. Checkerboard floors, gray walls elsewhere in the room.

Stairs

Connecting space between the living room and bedrooms upstairs. Reclaimed hardwood treads, milled with a built-up roundover nose, stained to match Zayne's warm tan tone and finished in a hard multi-coat clear, over risers faced in Edward Martin Leona 24"x48" matte porcelain, Calacatta — cut to full-width strips for durability against toe scuffs and vacuum hits. Walls gray, glossy finish. Handrail white; all other hardware in matte black.

Under-Stairs Walk-In Closet

An empty under-stairs closet, fitted out with a mix of hanging rods and open shelving, a wall-mounted vacuum charging dock, and a dedicated light fixture. General-purpose storage. Checkerboard floor, gray walls in glossy finish, matte black hardware.
